intro.text: In Vorin society, people with dark eyes, usually brown or black: the commoners, ranked below the lighteyes.

description.text: Darkeyes of the first and second nahn are full citizens with the right of travel and can even marry into lighteyed families. A wealthy, high-ranking darkeyes is addressed as Citizen, while lighteyes rarely call a darkeyes "darkborn", a term implying contempt.

Darkeyes are ranked by nahn, the counterpart of the lighteyes' dahn. Any nahn is socially below the lowest dahn, though circumstances can blur this: as a captain, darkeyed Kaladin held authority over lighteyed soldiers who outranked him socially.
Darkeyes of high enough nahn who serve an essential role in a town can be exempt from conscription, and may get a commission to work unused land and keep part of the crop.
A Vorin legend says that a man who wins a Shardblade in battle becomes a lighteyes, regardless of his station, and is raised to the fourth dahn.

items.text: Hoid feels he should be amused at the importance given to eye colour, but isn't: he has seen other arbitrary systems, and remembers there is a good reason the belief in lighteyed superiority arose.
For the first time in generations a darkeyes became a Shardbearer, and so rose to the fourth dahn, when Moash received a full set of Shards from Kaladin.
Swearing Ideals can also lighten the eyes: when Kaladin swore the Third Ideal at the Battle of Narak, his eyes turned pale blue, lighter than any king's.
The right of travel was suggested by Nale, who helped scribes write the laws on eye colour.
